I was tasked with running a food thing at a carnival, and what I did was very successful, and not hard.

the non food equipment needed is a fondue pot, and sticks.

the product is chocolate covered bananas rolled in peanuts.

I didn't, but if you want to go gourmet, your can introduce white chocolate, and of course candy and shit. I just did peanuts and chocolate and they sold out in a second, so I had someone rush out and get me another 200 pounds of bananas, all sold. I looked into wholesale bananas but its not doable for smaller business endeavors like a truck. check out the business model though:

banana price per pound (stable around 60cents US per pound. 1 pound = three medium sized bananas)

1 banana = $0.20 10 pounds of chocolate= $60 http://www.amazon.com/Hersheys-Milk-Chocolate-Candy-5-Pound/dp/B000IW68YC 10 pounds of ready-to-go peanuts= $30 http://www.amazon.com/Roasted-Chopped-Peanuts-Pound-Case/dp/B001ESHO88/ref=sr_1_1?s=grocery&ie=UTF8&qid=1435572431&sr=1-1&keywords=peanuts+10pounds

if you load each banana up with peanuts and chocolate, 10 pounds of each will make you 3000 bananas worth of these delicious treats.

3000 bananas = $600 retail. talk to your local grocery store chains if you make this a regular thing and try to get in on some of their wholesale action. I'm sure you know how to handle that, but I put the retail price for start up, to show its viability.

Now that you've spent your start up costs on ingredients, it's time to start dipping bananas! It's not hard. cut a banana in half, and if you can try to cut out the bruised parts if possible, people hate those. not necessary but it makes for a good first impression of your product. Take a lesson from the Japanese here and you'll find people flocking back for return business based on their impression of your quality (over efficiency. something I feel is lacking in some Canadian businesses).

sell each half banana for a dollar.

revenue: $6000 cost: $690 * 1.5 = 1035 (though I didn't incur any costs above this it's always a good idea to multiply costs by 1.5 for hidden costs when planning.)

profit: ~$5000, with a mark up of 870%

I just ran a small one for charity when I was in uni, but it raised more money than any other initiative, $800 in the one night I ran it for (at a carnvial night attended by approximately 2000 people. I was limited only by the number of bananas and my dreams.). Think about it. would you eat one? right now if I make you one fresh? would a fat person? for me, the answer is yes to all three. these things are good, but it's not something you can easily make just a single person's worth of at home, so you can mark it up like mad, and people are still happy to pay you a bit of change because it's that or never eat one. which would fatty choose?

bonus things I would do if I took this business model further:

The most lacking thing that held my operation back was the lack of a disposable banana stick holder. its really hard to buy more than one for each person receiving the bananas due to the number of hands. you can maybe thing of a cool design, or just buy blocks of styrofoam. design considerations: must stand up by itself when set on a table. must hold at least 6 banana sticks. must not fall down (styrofoam may be too light to satisfy this).

$18/ 5lbs White chocolate: http://www.amazon.com/Clasens-Alpine-Coatings-Brite-Chocolate/dp/B009K172YM/ref=sr_1_5?s=grocery&ie=UTF8&qid=1435573613&sr=1-5&keywords=white+chocolate+5lbs

$24/ 7lbs Colourful sprinkles for fats or children: http://www.amazon.com/Chefs-Quality-Rainbow-Sprinkles-lb/dp/B00J3Z46W6/ref=sr_1_1?s=grocery&ie=UTF8&qid=1435573545&sr=1-1&keywords=bulk+sprinkles

That's all you need for variety. the extra $350 dollars budgeted might be useful for satisfying health regulations in your state with regards to serving food from a truck, or to developing a side product. you can fondue anything, as long as it's cheap. I reccommened Chocolate Covered Marshmallow Beetus Sticks (new name pending), for cost effectiveness. or if you are feeling fancy, here's a recipe i just made up based on what I could find for cheap-ish on amazon:

one marshmallow dip in in chocolate roll it in graham cracker crumbs

A new twist on an old classic, s'mores globs that don't get crumbs all over your shirt.

$100 cost for 400servings, sold for one dollar each that's a 400% mark up. not as profitable as bananas, but it has the bonus of the ingredients never going bad, and more options for no more work.
